study_identification_part.si4_title: Dynamic gray matter volume changes in pediatric multiple sclerosis: A 3.5 year MRI study

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives in the Abstract ('Objectives') to assess spatial patterns of GM atrophy, their dynamic changes over time, and clinical relevance. The Methods specify the purpose of applying normative modeling: estimating deviations from age- and sex-specific normative GM developmental trajectories and relating deviation scores to disability, IQ, and lesion volumes. Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: Objectives: To assess, using MRI, the spatial patterns of gray matter (GM) atrophy in pediatric patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), their dynamic changes over time, and their clinical relevance. Methods: ... a group of 317 pediatric HC ... was used to estimate GM developmental trajectories. In pediatric patients with MS, deviations from normative GM volume values at the voxel level were assessed ... Correlations between GM volume deviations and disability, IQ, and white matter (WM) lesion volumes (LV) were estimated.

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: They build a new normative model using pediatric HC from the NIH MRI Study of Normal Brain Development. Eligibility/details are described for both HC sources: local HSR HC had no neurologic dysfunction and normal exam; for NIH HC, they performed an image quality check for motion/other artifacts and report the final sample size (n=317) with follow-up counts. This meets: eligibility described (with source cited), IQC specified, final sample size reported. While counts excluded are not enumerated, reasons for exclusion (motion/artifacts) are stated.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: HSR HC: '... 26 sex- and age-matched HC ... with no history of neurologic dysfunction and a normal neurologic examination ...' NIH HC: 'MRI data from all available HC were initially downloaded, then an image quality check for motion and other artifacts was performed. From the final 317 NIH HC dataset considered suitable for the analysis, a subset was followed up once (n = 163) and another twice (n = 154) ...'

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates including age, sex, age×sex interaction, and age^2 are modeled in a voxel-wise linear mixed-effects framework; they also include a binary covariate to account for magnetic field strength (MFS)/acquisition protocol, addressing multi-site/sequence differences. This satisfies covariate handling and site/acquisition effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: 'To estimate normative sex- and age-expected GM growth curves, using Matlab's 'fitlme' function ... the following linear mixed-effects model was fitted voxel-wise ...' and 'Another binary variable to account for differences in magnetic field strength (MFS) and acquisition protocol was also added ...' Also: 'MFS showed the lowest absolute r values (median [IQR] ... age, sex, age × sex, age^2, MFS ...).'

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described in detail: SPM12 longitudinal registration, segmentation, DARTEL template creation/normalization, Jacobian modulation, and 4-mm Gaussian smoothing. Lesion refilling is applied prior to GM volumetrics. Software tools are specified.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: 'Within-subject serial longitudinal registration as implemented in SPM12 ... segmented ... DARTEL registration ... an affine transformation ... midpoint average templates were intensity modulated ... each group of timepoints ... was spatially normalized (DARTEL), modulated, and smoothed with a 4-mm Gaussian kernel ... The result ... was a modulated, smoothed, and normalized GM image ...' and '... underwent lesion refilling before GM volumetric analysis.'

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No hold-out, cross-validation, or other partitioning strategy for internal validation of the normative model is described. The linear mixed-effects trajectories are estimated on the HC cohort without mention of testing on unseen HC within iterations.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: '... the following linear mixed-effects model was fitted voxel-wise to HC preprocessed GM maps' (no description of train/test splits or cross-validation).

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model is applied to pediatric MS patients to compute z-scores; there is no application to an independent external healthy dataset for validation separate from model development.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: 'In pediatric patients with MS, deviations from normative GM volume values at the voxel level were assessed at baseline and during the follow-up ...'

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: They specify the statistical framework (voxel-wise linear mixed-effects modeling), key model terms (age, sex, interactions, age^2), random effects (subject intercept/slope implied), adjustment for MFS/acquisition, and implementation software (Matlab 'fitlme'). Z-scores are computed from the estimated mean and SD.
